title: How Trains Turn Without Steering 🚆 #shorts
description:
A train's two wheels are locked to one solid axle, so they always spin at the same speed. So how does it get around a curve where the outer rail is longer? The wheels are cones. In a curve the wheelset shifts outward, the outer wheel rolls on its wider part and the inner wheel on its narrower part, and the axle steers itself around the bend. The same cones keep it centred on straight track, until at high speed the correction overshoots into a side-to-side wobble engineers call hunting.

Follow Hidden Mechanics for more everyday engineering, explained in under a minute.
